propositions: rebar's ticket store push.py performs a git stash->merge->pop dance in the tickets worktree, which can apply stash entries created by other worktrees because the stash stack is shared across all repository worktrees
a stash entry created on a source worktree can be popped into the tickets worktree, leaving the index stranded with unmerged entries and corrupting the store with non-ticket source files
the stash dance assumes all stashed edits are reconciler-regenerable, but this assumption does not hold when foreign stashes are applied, causing real ticket data conflicts and write failures

the tickets worktree index can be left stranded with unmerged entries pointing to source paths that do not belong on the tickets branch, blocking every subsequent store write until manual intervention
rebar must replace the stash->merge->pop mechanism with a worktree-scoped design (e.g. stash create by sha, reset, merge, stash apply by sha) that cannot touch the shared stash stack
a supported maintenance entrypoint must exist with backup-before-first-write, refusal on unpushed commits, durable audit records, and a break-glass override for edge cases
